catalog_quote: Baṭḥari has word stress accent, meaning that a combination of vowel lengthening, change in pitch and intensity contribute to give prominence to one and only one syllable for each lexeme. ... According to what Johnstone (1975: 10) states about Mehri, “long vowels occur only in stressed open syllables or stressed final-VVC syllables”. This general rule can be held true also for Baṭḥari. ... This means that long vowels can appear only in stressed CV or CVC final syllables. ... There are only two conditions which allow the presence of a long vowel in an unstressed syllable, namely: i. the presence of /ʕ/ itself, or ii. the presence of a glide as one of the root consonants. ... To conclude, accent and vowel length are connected and are conditioned by these two constraints: i. a stressed vowel is always lengthened (but a long vowel is not always stressed); ii. a stressed vowel in any closed s…

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every fragment of the deciding quotation is verbatim in the held Gasparini 2018 thesis text at the stated printed pages (43, 45-46), and the §5.1.3 pronoun-class locator is also confirmed (pp. 68-69). (2) Deciding source: a 2018 PhD thesis 'towards' a grammar, serious and first-hand, whose stress section explicitly treats vowel length as a consequence of stress and states no placement rule, so the 'morphological/lexical, no positional rule' coding is a fair reading of it. But it is no longer the best description: the same author has since co-published the full reference grammar (Morris & Gasparini 2025, Semitica Viva 66, 518 pp; confirmed on the Harrassowitz page, in Gasparini's ORCID works list, in the held Wikipedia raw, and by a 2026 JSS review) plus a 2025 JSS feature survey; neither is open access and we hold neither.
